steps.response: Served the purpose. ShipLoop's rerun refused 3 of 10 rows on SLChessRulesTest.controllerIllegalMove. The failing assertion showed that AuraHandledException.getMessage() lacks the move name unless setMessage is called (anonymous Apex could not throw it, so the test was the probe). The model fixed the controller, 14/6/3 passed, and the item was accepted as d53e06cd. This overturned the implement Improve's recorded decision 'Do not add setMessage' (23 review-1).

Proof: check-only first refused for a missing result, then reran all 10 recorded rows (refused 3/10), then accepted after the fix; complete reran them again and accepted. Review: verify's own Until Loop ran iteration 1, non-trivial (new test plus setMessage), and iteration 2, a trivial recheck. Rows 7-9 repeat rows 1-3, so each full rerun deployed 6 times for 3 classes (known D-1).

run_level.step_by_step: Group 26-38 is the tail of the one item W1 plus the outer release sequence. W1 (its 3 planned steps had collapsed into one at 16/17) was verified once: check-only ran all 10 recorded rows (refused 3/10 on controllerIllegalMove), then accepted after the fix, and complete reran them and accepted (d53e06cd). The review was verify's own 2-iteration loop, then carry-forward plus Improve 28. The outer stages then ran strictly in plan order, with no skip and no out-of-order stage: system-test-author, Improve 30, system-test, product-acceptance, release-plan, Improve 34, release-check, release, release-verify. Each had a script-run proof where one exists: system-test's rerun of 4 rows, the release-check --dry-run file, the release deploy receipt, the release-verify Tooling queries. Only release-verify repeated, blocking twice, and the run ended there.
run_level.improve: Three Improves ran 4 passes, and 1 of them found something real. Pass 1 of 34 found the architecture allow-list row giving the deploy to release-check; the fix (dc5ab465) held, since release-check only dry-ran and release made the one deploy. Cost: 78 + 417 + 236 s, 99 calls, and 18 ShipLoop-source reads, almost all spent on the Improve route itself (skill-call gate, FOCUS_IDS, uncommitted HOME edits, next_argv), not on the product. Misses: (1) all three read HOME/architecture.md ## Real-boundary checks, and 34 edited a row of that table, yet none saw that its promotion line is unplayable (a6 a7 is blocked by Black's a7 pawn) or that its FEN checks are invisible to a person; both went to the owner at 37/38. (2) 34 restated 'source return is a fast-forward', which release-check disproved. (3) 30's first pass was a rubber stamp, judged trivial before reading and misreading green TAP as '6 failed, 3 skipped'; only a compaction forced a real redo.
